Coffee___Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.diseaseName: Cercospora leaf spot / brown eye spot (Cercospora coffeicola)
symptoms: Small round brown spots with a pale grey or white centre and a yellow halo, like an eye
Dark, sunken, dry patches on berries, which may ripen early
Leaves drop early when many spots are present
Coffee___Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Improve plant nutrition, especially nitrogen, and reduce water stress. Copper-based fungicides help protect new growth. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Remove and destroy heavily spotted leaves and berries

symptoms: No visible signs of disease or pest damage
Coffee___Healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep monitoring, especially during the rains.
prevention: Check leaves weekly for rust, spots and mines

symptoms: Irregular brown dried blotches (mines) on the upper leaf surface
The dried skin of the mine peels off, with small larvae inside
Heavy attack causes leaves to fall
possibleCauses: pest damage: moth larvae feeding inside the leaf
natural enemies killed by broad-spectrum sprays
Coffee___Leaf_Miner.treatment: Count active mines before spraying; many attacks are controlled by natural parasites. If damage is heavy, use an insecticide recommended by your extension officer and avoid broad-spectrum products. Ask your agrovet for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Protect natural enemies by avoiding unnecessary sprays
Keep some shade and ground cover

symptoms: Dark brown to black patches, often at leaf tips and edges
Young leaves and shoot tips turn black and die back
Worse after cold, wet and windy weather
possibleCauses: cold wet weather at high altitude
Coffee___Phoma.treatment: Prune out and destroy dead shoot tips. Copper-based fungicides protect new growth during cold wet periods. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Protect new flushes during cold wet seasons

symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery spots on the underside of leaves
Pale yellow patches on the upper side above the powder
Leaves fall early and branches may die back
possibleCauses: fungal infection spread by wind and rain splash
Coffee___Rust.treatment: Copper-based fungicides protect leaves; systemic fungicides may be recommended where rust is severe. Timing matters, so follow your extension officer's spray calendar. Ask your agrovet for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant varieties such as Ruiru Eleven or Batian
Prune and space trees for air flow

symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves, often with a yellow halo
Spots join up and leaves turn yellow and dry
Small raised scabby spots on green fruit
Tomato___Bacterial_Spot.treatment: There is no cure. Remove badly infected plants. Copper-based bactericides can slow the spread. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and seedlings
Rotate away from tomato, pepper and potato
Avoid overhead watering and do not work among wet plants

symptoms: Brown spots with rings inside like a target, on older lower leaves first
Yellowing around the spots; leaves dry and fall
Dark sunken patches on stems and near the fruit stalk
possibleCauses: warm weather with dew or rain
Tomato___Early_Blight.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves. Protectant fungicides such as mancozeb or chlorothalonil, or a recommended systemic, slow the disease. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Rotate crops and remove old crop debris
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves
Stake plants and keep good spacing

symptoms: No visible signs of disease or pest damage
Tomato___Healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep monitoring, especially in wet weather.
prevention: Check leaves twice a week in the rains
Water at the base, not over the leaves

symptoms: Large grey-green water-soaked patches that quickly turn brown
White fuzzy growth under the leaves in wet weather
Firm brown patches on fruit; whole plants can collapse within days
possibleCauses: nearby infected tomato or potato crops
Tomato___Late_Blight.treatment: Act quickly: remove and destroy infected plants away from the field. Fungicides with metalaxyl or cymoxanil, alongside a protectant such as mancozeb, are commonly recommended. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Do not plant tomato next to potato
Use tolerant varieties and wide spacing
Start protective sprays before long rains as advised by extension

symptoms: Pale green or yellow patches on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mould under the leaves
Mostly in greenhouses and very humid conditions
possibleCauses: high humidity and poor air flow
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Lower humidity by opening vents and spacing plants. Remove infected leaves. Fungicides may be needed if it spreads. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Prune lower leaves for air flow

symptoms: Light and dark green patchy mottling on leaves
Leaves twisted, narrow or fern-like
Stunted plants with fewer, uneven fruit
possibleCauses: virus spread by hands, tools and infected seed
Tomato___Mosaic_Virus.treatment: There is no cure. Uproot and destroy infected plants early. Wash hands and disinfect tools before handling healthy plants.
prevention: Use certified seed and resistant varieties
Do not smoke or handle tobacco near the crop
Disinfect tools and stakes between seasons

symptoms: Many small round spots with dark brown edges and grey or tan centres
Tiny black dots inside the spots; unlike early blight there are no target rings
Starts on lower leaves, which yellow and fall
possibleCauses: warm wet weather and rain splash
Tomato___Septoria_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves. Protectant fungicides such as mancozeb or chlorothalonil slow the spread. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Rotate crops and clear old plants
Mulch and water at the base
Control weeds such as nightshade that carry the fungus

symptoms: Brown spots with rings and a yellow halo, easily confused with early blight
Spots can merge and dry large parts of the leaf
Small sunken brown spots on fruit
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve air flow. Fungicides may be needed. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Prune and stake for air flow

symptoms: Leaves curl upward and cup, with yellow edges
Young leaves small and crumpled
Stunted plants; flowers drop and few fruit form
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no cure. Uproot infected plants early. Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps and an insecticide recommended by your extension officer. Ask your agrovet for the product and rate registered in Kenya.

symptoms: Sunken round spots on fruit with rings of orange or pink spores
Small irregular brown spots on leaves
Fruit rots, especially when ripening
Pepper___Anthracnose.treatment: Pick and destroy infected fruit. Fungicides can protect healthy fruit. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Harvest promptly and avoid wounding fruit

symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown
Leaves yellow and drop
Raised scabby spots on fruit
Pepper___Bacterial_Spot.treatment: There is no cure. Remove infected plants. Copper-based bactericides can slow the spread. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Rotate away from pepper and tomato

symptoms: No visible signs of disease or pest damage
Patchy light and dark green mottling
Leaves narrow, distorted or wrinkled
Stunted plants and misshapen fruit
possibleCauses: virus spread by hands and tools
Pepper___Mosaic_Virus.treatment: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected plants. Control aphids with a method recommended by your extension officer.
prevention: Use tolerant varieties and clean seedlings
Remove weeds that host the virus

symptoms: Angular brown spots boxed in by leaf veins
Grey fuzzy growth under the spots in humid weather
Reddish-brown spots on pods
Bean___Angular_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove badly infected plants. Fungicides may help in wet seasons. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.

symptoms: Dark red to black streaks along the veins under the leaves
Sunken dark spots on pods with pink or tan centres
Spotted, discoloured seed
Bean___Anthracnose.treatment: Remove infected plants. Fungicides can protect the crop in wet weather. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Plant certified clean seed, never seed from infected pods
Do not work in the field when plants are wet

symptoms: No visible signs of disease or pest damage
Small reddish-brown powdery spots, mostly under the leaves
Yellow rings around the spots
Leaves dry and fall early
Bean___Rust.treatment: Fungicides can slow rust when applied early. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Avoid planting next to an infected crop

symptoms: Dark brown spots with target-like rings on older leaves
Yellowing around the spots
Shallow dark patches on tubers
Potato___Early_Blight.treatment: Protectant fungicides such as mancozeb slow the disease. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.

symptoms: No visible signs of disease or pest damage
Potato___Healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep monitoring, especially for late blight in wet weather.
prevention: Check leaves twice a week in the rains

symptoms: Large dark water-soaked patches on leaves that spread fast
White fuzzy growth under leaves in wet weather
Brown rot inside tubers
Potato___Late_Blight.treatment: Act quickly: destroy infected plants. Fungicides with metalaxyl or cymoxanil, alongside a protectant such as mancozeb, are commonly recommended. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
prevention: Use certified seed and tolerant varieties
Hill up soil to protect tubers
Start protective sprays before long rains as advised by extension

symptoms: Reddish-brown water-soaked patches on young leaves and shoots
Shoots and flowers dry and die back
Dark sunken spots on cashew apples and nuts
possibleCauses: wet humid weather at flushing and flowering
Cashew___Anthracnose.treatment: Prune and destroy infected shoots. Fungicides protect new flushes. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.

symptoms: Gum oozing from cracks in the trunk and branches
Bark darkens and splits around the gum
Branches wilt and die back
Cashew___Gummosis.treatment: Scrape away diseased bark and treat the wound as advised by your extension officer. Remove dead branches. Ask your agrovet for the product registered in Kenya.

symptoms: No visible signs of disease or pest damage
Cashew___Healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep monitoring at flushing and flowering.

symptoms: Silvery blisters on tender young leaves
Blisters dry and leaves crumple
Young flushes look scorched
possibleCauses: pest damage: moth larvae feeding inside young leaves
Cashew___Leaf_Miner.treatment: Protect new flushes if damage is heavy, using an insecticide recommended by your extension officer. Ask your agrovet for the product and rate registered in Kenya.

Cashew___Red_Rust.diseaseName: Red rust (algal leaf spot, Cephaleuros virescens)
symptoms: Rusty orange velvety spots on the upper leaf surface
Spots are raised and round
Heavily covered leaves turn yellow
Cashew___Red_Rust.treatment: Prune to let in light and air. Copper-based products are commonly recommended. Ask your agrovet or extension officer for the product and rate registered in Kenya.
